The family does verbalize willingness to *********.     Family History:     There is no other reported medical history in the family other than dad having been diagnosed with a 'coronary artery defect' at the age of 20. However, dad reports that his extended family includes several family members with a history of alcohol abuse.  There is no ******* history of DV or involvement with DCF.       Adherence:  The only concern related to adherence is *****'s difficulty taking her medications.  She has demonstrated difficulty taking them at times while admitted, and has vomited after taking them a few times.  Parents report that she sometimes does better taking them when they administer, but sometimes does not.  They state she seems to do better taking them when she is at home, as she knows she needs to do so to prevent a return trip to the hospital.  However, they admit that taking meds on a schedule (as is needed post-transplant) will be a new experience for all of them.  They verbalize understanding that there will be a lot of meds initially, that are gradually reduced.  They verbalize belief that they will be able to get her to take them, especially if she is advised of what they do and how important they are.       The family denies that there will be any difficulty keeping follow up appointments, obtaining labs, etc.       Assessment and recommendations:     The family is adjusting to the information regarding *****'s medical condition.  This is all relatively new to the family.  The parents disclosed that they are struggling with some self-blame, as she did not have any problems prior to the first surgery in ****. They question if she would have been ok if they had not agreed to surgery at that time.  However, the verbalize understanding that they have to move past that, and deal with the current situation.  At this point, they verbalize that **** ***** ** ******** and are aware that there is nothing surgically that can be done to make *****'s heart improve.  They are in agreement with moving forward with transplant.  However, they do not appear to understand fully what transplant involves.  They appear to need medical things to be broken down in very simple terms.  They are also hesitant about explaining transplant to *****.  SW explained that it is best to be ******* with children her age, as this increases the child's trust in the adults involved in her care.  Unfortunately, she is currently intubated and sedated and will likely not be able to be prepared for the ****** prior to waking up with it.  SW explained that this can be traumatic initially for a child who does not understand what happened.  Parents verbalize willingness to let ********* assist ***** in processing this.  They are also amenable to counseling as soon as the financial/ insurance part can be worked out.       The parents disclosed that *****'s medical condition is already having a significant impact on their family. They report that their 7 year old son who is autistic has begun acting out at school, and is repeatedly asking where ***** is.  They similarly report that their 5 year old is asking for *****.  In addition, they report that the family did not get to do anything over the ****** as a result of *****'s admissions, and are concerned that the other children may begin to resent the time the parents have to spend at the hospital.  Similarly, their oldest was unable to begin attending ******* ** planned, as the family did not move to ******* area as anticipated.  As a result, she is doing on-line classes instead.       Ultimately, the family expresses that they will do whatever it takes for *****, and believe their faith will support them through whatever the future holds.                IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  2     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 2     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  2     Coping Skills - 2     Total:  15  Low/Moderate     The family scores as low to moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concerns are the financial stressors and the difficulty ***** has demonstrated with taking oral medications.
